subject: Streaming p95 & concurrency -- recap + proposed next steps
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Joel Park <joel@fastwallet.com>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Streaming p95 & concurrency -- recap + proposed next steps

Hi Joel — thanks again for the call this morning. Attached is a short recap and suggested next steps so we can scope a short trial around your streaming checkout flow. TL;DR: primary pain is tail latency at peak concurrency, goal is p95 <= 250ms for streaming / interactive checks, and you want explicit concurrency controls and graceful fallbacks (cheaper model when overloaded).

Key points from our discussion:
- Current stack: FastWallet front-end -> in-house gateway -> batching layer -> single model endpoint (larger LLM) for both short prompts (3–10 tokens generation) and longer receipts parsing flows. You confirmed batching increases average throughput but amplifies tail latency under bursty trafic.
- Pain: p95 spikes to 700–900ms at peak traffic (holiday spikes), which causes UI stalls and checkout abandonment.
- Success criteria: p95 streaming (for the short, interactive checks) consistently <= 250ms at 99 concurrent sessions in our environment; acceptable median <= 80ms; fallbacks < 150ms added latency when triggered.
- Constraints: token budget per request ~60 tokens; requests are latency-sensitive, cannot queue for more than ~100ms before user-perceivable delay.

Proposal / next steps:
1) Nikhil to run a quick profiling pass on your sample trace (you shared system_trace_20270518.log) and propose 2 config options: (A) low-latency single-request config with small batch sizes + KV cache prewarm, (B) cost-favoring config with 8-token micro-batching and async streaming. ETA 2 business days.
2) Marissa to spin up a 48-hour pilot configuration on Redwood Dedicated (isolated pool) with both configs, synthetic replay of your peak hour, and built-in tracing. We’ll provide a perf dashboard and token-level cost breakdown. ETA pilot start: Tue 05/25, outcome within 72 hours.
3) Joel / FastWallet to provide a 1-hour sample trace (production redacted) and confirmation of expected peak concurrency window; also confirm whether you can accept a model fallback to a smaller/quantized variant for non-critical checks.
4) Schedule a 30-min sync after the pilot results to pick a rollout path.

Attachments: fastwallet-current-architecture.png (diagram), system_trace_20270518.log (log stub), trial_spec.xlsx (pilot acceptance criteria).

Thanks — I’ll queue Nikhil and Marissa on the profiling work now.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Re: Streaming p95 & concurrency -- recap + proposed next steps

Laura — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming a few items from our side:
- We can share a redacted 1-hour trace from Tuesday 05/18 (I attached it to the reply) — it contains headers showing per-request queue time, batch size distribution, and downstream processing time.
- Peak concurrency: typically 90–120 concurrent checkout sessions during promos (US evening).
- We are open to a fallback to a smaller quantized model for non-critical validation (content classification checks), but fraud-scoring must stay on the larger model.
- Acceptance criteria: If your pilot shows sustained p95 <= 250ms for the interactive path at 100 concurrent sessions with no >1% error increase, we’ll greenlight a staged rollout.

Two quick asks: can you confirm whether Redwood’s Dedicated pool will allow us to pin capacity for peak windows (we’d prefer a burst policy we control), and how function/tool-calling works with streaming responses (we have a microservice that expects partial tokens to flow immediately).

I’ll accept the pilot schedule. Thanks — Joel

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 12:25:00 -07:00
Subject: FW: Streaming p95 & concurrency -- profiling notes (internal)

Laura / Marissa — quick internal note after scanning Joel's trace. High-level observations:
- Batch-induced tail: we see long tail on requests where batching waits for 2–3 more tokens before dispatch; those cluster during burst windows. Suggest configuring dynamic batching thresholds by endpoint (interactive path: immediate dispatch when queue wait > 20ms).
- KV cache warmup: many requests hit cold KV cache for personalized tokens; prewarming popular prefixes reduces early-token latency.
- Model choice: recommend trying a quantized 7B variant for fallback (roughly 3–4x cheaper and tail-friendly) while keeping 13B for fraud scoring.

Proposed quick experiments (I’ll attach a short spec):
1) Micro-batching policy A: max batch time 20ms, max batch size 8, immediate dispatch for interactive-tagged requests.
2) Dedicated pool config B: provision 2x GPU units during promo windows with burst policy = +20% capacity auto-scale; pinable to FastWallet.
3) Streaming hook test: ensure partial token flushes within 30ms of generation for front-end streaming consumer.

I’ll prepare trial_spec.xlsx with the exact trace replay steps and pass to Marissa to deploy the pilot. ETA profile notes + config draft: EOD tomorrow.

-Nikhil

Joel — great, thanks for confirming. Two quick clarifications and then we’ll kick off the pilot:
1) Dedicated pool: yes — we can provision a Dedicated pool for FastWallet with a customer-controlled burst window (we’ll include instructions for pinning extra capacity and an auto-scale guardrail). I’ll loop in Sales Ops if you want a formal quote for reserved capacity options.
2) Streaming + function hooks: Redwood streams partial tokens as they are generated and supports immediate tool/function-calls; we’ll validate that partial token latency meets your 30ms flush target during the pilot.

Action items (owners + ETA):
- Joel: upload redacted 1-hour trace to the Drive link and confirm the typical promo window hours (by EOD 05/20).
- Nikhil: deliver profiling report and two config options (ETA 05/21 EOD).
- Marissa: schedule pilot on Redwood Dedicated to start Tue 05/25, and configure tracing + dashboard (will confirm pilot playbook by 05/21).

I’ll send calendar invites for the pilot kickoff and the post-pilot review. Thanks everyone — excited to get this running.
